title: Avoiding Expensive Expressions and Unnecessary Work knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes “Avoiding Expensive Expressions and Unnecessary Work”?
options: Built-in functions turn values into the form a query needs. Confirm return types, NULL behavior, timezone assumptions, rounding, and edge cases before using a result in application logic.
It is a frontend styling feature and does not involve database behavior.
It guarantees correct output regardless of schema, permissions, or release version.
It is best handled by removing constraints and skipping error checks.
questions.answer_key: Built-in functions turn values into the form a query needs. Confirm return types, NULL behavior, timezone assumptions, rounding, and edge cases before using a result in application logic.
questions.explanation: The lesson explains: Built-in functions turn values into the form a query needs. Confirm return types, NULL behavior, timezone assumptions, rounding, and edge cases before using a result in application logic.

questions.prompt: Which practice best applies “Avoiding Expensive Expressions and Unnecessary Work” safely?
options: Skip testing, assume every SQL engine behaves identically, and apply the change directly to production.
Concatenate untrusted input into SQL text and grant administrator privileges to every application user.
Judge success only by whether the statement returns any rows, without checking expected behavior or edge cases.
Predict the output type and value, run a minimal SELECT expression, and test a NULL or boundary input.
questions.answer_key: Predict the output type and value, run a minimal SELECT expression, and test a NULL or boundary input.
questions.explanation: Predict the output type and value, run a minimal SELECT expression, and test a NULL or boundary input. This makes the result reviewable and aligns with a controlled learning workflow.

questions.prompt: Before relying on an example for “Avoiding Expensive Expressions and Unnecessary Work”, what should be verified?

Assume a successful connection means the query and data model are correct.
Confirm the exact MySQL version and prerequisites, predict the result, run a minimal test in a disposable environment, then inspect the evidence and relevant official documentation.
Run a broad production change before checking the current state.
questions.answer_key: Confirm the exact MySQL version and prerequisites, predict the result, run a minimal test in a disposable environment, then inspect the evidence and relevant official documentation.
questions.explanation: Confirm the exact MySQL version and prerequisites, predict the result, run a minimal test in a disposable environment, then inspect the evidence and relevant official documentation.
